PullRequest.Title: fix add file to chat
PullRequest.Body:
- if no file is open, open the `+`
- removes duplicate command

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Add File to Chat with no eligible resource, including while Quick Open is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing AttachResourceAction first awaits chat-widget revelation. The new branch then awaits cancel(), which synchronously hides Quick Input, and dispatches the already-registered Add Context command. AttachContextAction checks registered items serially before showing the picker. Transcript-progress gating can return without showing it. Clipboard eligibility can delay initial picker display; file-query cache loading is not awaited by the display path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential extension activation for onCommand:workbench.action.chat.attachContext before executing the registered command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional command dispatch per empty-resource invocation. No interested extension means no IPC; otherwise activation is sent to extension-host managers and completed activation is reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The empty-resource branch returned after widget revelation. Explicitly invoking the existing Add Context command already used this dispatch path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potentially awaited after extension registration; not awaited when the extension host is not ready. The command is registered alongside Add File to Chat, so the unknown-command star-activation fallback is not reached.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read native clipboard image, encode it to PNG, and return its bytes to determine clipboard-item eligibility
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one eligibility read for the default clipboard item per picker opening, conditional on image attachment support, model vision capability, and readImageOnEnable. Browser implementation instead reads the clipboard and materializes a blob buffer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No clipboard eligibility read from the former empty-resource return. Opening the existing + context picker already performed exactly this check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited in the existing serial eligibility loop before showing the picker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit user command, the registered context-item collection, and optionally clipboard-image bytes; not workspace-file-count worth of clipboard or command calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: cancel() precedes command dispatch. Context-item eligibility is serial. Clipboard is one conditional read, not a per-file fan-out. Existing Quick Access lifecycle owns the displayed picker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Quick Input controllers and Quick Access providers are lazy singletons reused after first use. Command activation is skipped when completed or when no extension subscribes. Clipboard eligibility has no cache. Picker hide cancels unaccepted query work and disposes picker-owned resources.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added branch, registered target action, serial eligibility loop, clipboard implementation, and cancellation/disposal ownership were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Clipboard size and subscribed-extension activation latency vary; no timing measurements were collected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is explicit, user-requested entry into the existing attachment picker, not speculative background work. Its existing eligibility and initialization behavior is not newly amplified per picker opening. The async cancellation itself only hides the controller.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search for and select an attachment in the newly reachable context picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial picker display uses fast context/history picks without waiting for workspace enumeration. Typed file queries populate slow results. Selection separately awaits file/model/image resolution before adding the attachment; ordinary chat input is not blocked on background cache enumeration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate workspace roots and run grouped file searches through search providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A cache-load query when no equivalent cache is already updating, then generally one grouped search per effective nonempty query, or two when a multi-term search hits the limit. Each search validates F workspace folders and dispatches one provider call per URI scheme, not per returned file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The empty-resource command performed no search. Opening the existing context picker manually used the same query, grouping, cancellation, and cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache warming is off the initial display critical path. Search results await provider activation, root existence checks, and search completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward file-search queries to extension-host search providers when those providers own the resource scheme
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query RPC per participating provider/scheme for each issued search; result collection does not create per-file query RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No query RPC from the former empty-resource branch; the existing context picker already used the identical provider path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider completion is required for slow search results, not initial picker display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn ripgrep for local filesystem enumeration when a search requires a backend traversal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one process per local root requiring traversal, with existing exception/retry behavior; cached query results can avoid traversal. Roots are traversed concurrently, not one process per matching file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No enumeration from the former empty-resource return. Local searches through the existing context picker already used this engine.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background enumeration does not gate initial display; uncached result queries await their traversals.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat explicit path candidates and resolve parent directories to preserve filename casing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No calls for queries without path separators. Absolute paths use one candidate stat plus parent resolution on success; relative paths check at most one candidate per workspace folder, with parent resolution for successes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Absent from the former empty-resource branch; unchanged behavior of the existing requested picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Path checks gate corresponding slow results. Relative-folder checks are serial and run alongside the grouped workspace search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a selected text model, or read and resize a selected image, then install existing attachment watchers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected resource per ordinary accept. Existing text models can satisfy model-reference creation without another file read. Image selection reads that image; it does not preload every search result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The empty-resource command previously attached nothing. Selecting through the existing + picker already performed the same resource resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After user selection, completion is needed for attachment insertion; model references are disposed immediately after validation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F workspace roots, S resource schemes, effective typed queries after cancellation/coalescing, existing history, and selected-file bytes. Normal file-query results are capped at 512 before combination/deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SearchService validates roots with Promise.all and groups provider calls by scheme. The local engine concurrently traverses roots. Relative path checks are serial alongside the main search. Existing fast/slow picker scheduling and cancellation are unchanged; there is no diff-added per-result fan-out or new limiter removal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FileQueryCacheState preserves compatible previous cache keys while refreshing, avoids starting another load when an equivalent previous state is updating, and disposes replaced cache state. Loaded queries can use backend cached results, including cached narrowing. Cold typing uses the existing 200 ms throttled delayer; canceled work is checked before issuance and after awaits. Error states are distinct from loaded states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: picker initialization, fast/slow result separation, query cache lifecycle, provider grouping, local process traversal, path checks, and selection-only reads were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace size, root count, remote provider latency, clipboard state, and selected-file sizes vary. Provider-internal caching and performance differ by implementation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds a requested way to reach the existing search/selection workflow but does not change its effective cardinality, caching, concurrency, or resource lifecycle. Existing search and image-resolution opportunities are outside this diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attach an active file or explicit multi-file selection from an editor, Explorer, or search results
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget revelation and in-memory resource extraction are unchanged. Valid resources follow the existing focusInput/addFile loop; the new fallback is never entered. Text attachments are inserted synchronously, while image resolution remains asynchronously scheduled by the existing loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create local file watchers and, for supported local images, stat/read/resolve the image
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One watcher per newly inserted local attachment ID; existing attachment IDs are filtered before insertion. Image resolution is invoked per supplied image before attachment deduplication, exactly as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extraction, loop, deduplication, watchers, and image-resolution work occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watchers accompany insertion. Existing asynchronous image reads can continue after the action's unawaited addFile loop.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N explicitly supplied or selected resources and their image bytes; unchanged editor-context grouping and attachment-ID deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ordinary files are inserted in a synchronous loop; existing async image operations may overlap. No added await, boundary call, or concurrency change on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing attachments are deduplicated by ID; watcher ownership uses a DisposableMap and removes watchers on attachment removal or model disposal. The new service lookups do not access the lazy Quick Input controller on this branch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both diff and addFile implementation establish that valid-resource behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selection and image sizes vary, but their costs are not introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the changed code only obtains two services before resource extraction, without invoking the picker or adding expensive resource work on the successful attachment path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the legacy Copilot attachment command or open the Command Palette
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The legacy command still forwards through the extension command API to the core Add File command. The palette now omits the duplicate legacy entry; core-command visibility is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward github.copilot.chat.attachFile to workbench.action.chat.attachFile through the extension command API
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing forwarding execution per invocation of the legacy command. No forwarding occurs just because the palette is opened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical command registration and forwarding implementation; the added source line is only a comment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Legacy command execution waits for the core command; the new empty-resource picker branch then follows the scenarios above.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit legacy-command invocations and the palette command collection, reduced by one visible duplicate entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One forwarding call per legacy invocation; no new startup or palette-render fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registration/disposal ownership is unchanged. The package menu condition adds no cache or retained per-invocation state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the manifest diff hides one command and the extension implementation has no executable change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured palette-performance effect; removal of a single entry is not evidence of a substantive regression fix.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression or qualifying performance-regression fix: the manifest removes a duplicate visible entry without changing forwarding frequency or registration lifetime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the full four-file inventory and every diff page. Traced the new empty-resource fallback and existing picker initialization, conditional clipboard IPC/serialization, search-provider grouping and subprocess traversal, caches, cancellation/disposal, selection-time file reads, valid-file attachments, and legacy forwarding. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression and no concrete qualifying performance-regression fix were found. Static review; no measured durations.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
